title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 3 (Communication, acceptance and revocation of proposals)

content.overview: Section 3 provides that the communication of proposals, the acceptance of proposals, and the revocation of proposals and acceptances, respectively, are deemed to be made by any act or omission of the party proposing, accepting or revoking by which he intends to communicate such proposal, acceptance or revocation, or which has the effect of communicating it.
content.glance: Communication of proposal, acceptance or revocation is by any act or omission intending to communicate or having that effect.
content.study: Communication of proposals, of acceptances, and of revocations of proposals and acceptances is deemed to be made by any act or omission of the party proposing, accepting or revoking by which that party intends to communicate the proposal, acceptance or revocation, or which has the effect of communicating it. Section 3 is the general rule; timing of completion is under s. 4 and revocation under ss. 5–6. Current-law framing: identify the act or omission; test intention to communicate or effect of communicating; apply the deeming rule before analysing completion under s. 4.

sections.heading: What is communicated
sections.body: Proposals; acceptances of proposals; revocations of proposals and of acceptances.

sections.heading: How communication is made
sections.body: By any act or omission of the party proposing, accepting or revoking by which that party intends to communicate, or which has the effect of communicating.

provisions.title: Communication, acceptance and revocation of proposals

examples.title: Act communicating acceptance
examples.body: The offeree posts a letter of acceptance intending to communicate assent. Section 3 treats that act as the communication of acceptance (completion timing is under s. 4).

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 3 fix when communication is complete?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 3 states how communication is deemed made; when it is complete is governed by section 4.

distinctions.title: How communication is made (s. 3) vs when it is complete (s. 4)
distinctions.left: Act or omission intending to communicate or having that effect
distinctions.right: Knowledge / course of transmission rules for proposal, acceptance, revocation

misconceptions.trap: Only formal written notice counts as communication under the Act.
misconceptions.correction: Section 3 covers any act or omission intending to communicate or having the effect of communicating.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 3 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify proposal, acceptance or revocation. II. Find the act or omission. III. Test intention or effect of communicating. IV. Then apply s. 4 for completion. V. Conclude.

examTips: Note that omission can also communicate.
